claims.text: A 2–5 nm Al2O3 capping layer deposited by low-temperature ALD will modify interfacial strain in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type HEA thin films.
The Al2O3 capping layer will enhance thermal boundary conductance.
Changes in interfacial strain and thermal boundary conductance will influence magnetic domain-wall damping.
Changes in interfacial strain and thermal boundary conductance will influence magnetoelastic coupling.
Stress and heat-transfer changes caused by the oxide overlayer will reduce energy barriers for domain-wall motion.
Reduced barriers for domain-wall motion will reduce magnetic hysteresis.
More efficient cyclic heat extraction and reinjection will sharpen the magnetocaloric transition.
Capped films will exhibit lower magnetic hysteresis than uncapped films.
Capped films will exhibit a sharper magnetocaloric entropy-change response than uncapped films.
Capped films will exhibit a more reproducible magnetocaloric effect than uncapped films.
A capping thickness around 2–5 nm will provide the best balance of interfacial thermal properties and strain.
Capping layers significantly thinner or thicker than 2–5 nm may provide diminished magnetic-cooling performance.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type HEA films have a heterogeneous microstructure.
The low-dimensional films have degraded magnetocaloric behavior because of interfacial limitations.
The low-dimensional films have degraded magnetocaloric behavior because of heat-transfer limitations.
Uncapped as-deposited films typically have broader magnetocaloric transitions.
Uncapped as-deposited films typically have higher hysteresis because of suboptimal heat-transfer dynamics and uncontrolled interfacial stress.
The proposed intervention uses conformal Al2O3 deposited at temperatures below 150 °C.
The proposed test is restricted to applied magnetic fields below 0.1 T and temperatures from 300 K to 350 K.
